assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new platform for correlated and topological electrons: the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction at the magic angle was followed by correlated-insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opening the whole field of moire matter with tunable many-body physics. This is the kind of materials discovery where quantum mechanics keeps surprising us and theory and experiment are tightly linked.
assessment.attribution: Theory (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) and the 2018 experiments (Jarillo-Herrero group) are the decisive pair, and the three credited names form a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's experimental co-leads, notably Yuan Cao, are not in the credited list, which is a sensitivity.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced independently by many groups across twisted graphene and TMD moire systems; the interpretation of the superconductivity is still debated but the existence of flat-band correlated phases is firmly established. Timing is reasonable, about eight years after discovery.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene remains unsettled.
Experimental co-leads and early parallel theory work are not covered by the credited names, so the allocation of credit is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators are a genuinely new class of electronic matter, with protected edge and surface states, from the Kane-Mele proposal to the HgTe quantum spin Hall experiment and the spectroscopic identification of three-dimensional topological insulators. The impact on condensed-matter physics and on later quantum-materials work is large and lasting; it extends the topological-phase theme of the 2016 prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane (theory), Molenkamp (HgTe quantum spin Hall experiment) and Hasan (ARPES observation of 3D topological insulators, directly the type of spectroscopy-linked work I value) give a coherent three-person set. Eugene Mele's role in Kane-Mele and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (not credited) make this allocation contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by transport and spectroscopy in many materials; theory and ARPES agree quantitatively. Mature, with about two decades since the first observations.
uncertainties: Dropping Mele, who co-authored the foundational Kane-Mele papers, may be seen as unfair.
Overlaps with the separate quantum anomalous Hall candidate; the committee must decide the scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx and rapid extension to Tc above 50 K created a second family of high-temperature superconductors after the cuprates, with multiband and magnetic-fluctuation physics that DFT and spectroscopy have probed in detail. It is a clear, verified physical discovery.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 JACS paper by Kamihara, Hosono and co-workers is the clear origin; Hosono led the group. A two-person prize is clean, although the rapid follow-up from Chinese groups raising Tc is part of the story and not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently confirmed within months; the family is well characterised after about eighteen years. Theory has not converged on a pairing mechanism, but that does not weaken the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Practical impact is limited relative to the cuprates, and the follow-up work by others may weigh in credit discussions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, explaining the Mott transition and, combined with DFT, enabling quantitative materials calculations. As an electronic-structure theorist I regard it as one of the most important methods advances in the field.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt (and Metzner) introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to an impurity model and DMFT. The credited trio is a defensible configuration, but Walter Metzner, who is not in the credited names, is a genuine part of the origin, and the numerical solver developers also matter.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and validated against spectroscopy over three decades; cluster extensions and DFT+DMFT keep developing. Prizes for methods and theory are less frequent, and the committee tends to want clear experimental anchors.
uncertainties: Metzner's missing credit is an attribution problem.
Theory-method prizes need a strong link to measured phenomena; accuracy of DFT+DMFT for real materials is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the giant TMR with MgO barriers, underlies modern magnetic read heads and MRAM. It is a quantum-mechanical spin-dependent tunnelling discovery with large practical use, which the committee has precedent for rewarding (GMR, 2007).
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's work on MgO-based junctions and coherent tunnelling gave giant effects (with Yuasa and Djayaprawira in parallel, not credited). Credit for the giant-TMR MgO step is notably split, so the configuration is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature, commercially deployed for about two decades and extensively confirmed. Theory of coherent tunnelling (Butler, Mathon) agrees with measurements.
uncertainties: Yuasa and colleagues, the parallel MgO discovery, are outside the credited names.
Prize may be seen as an incremental extension of the 2007 GMR prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realisation of Hubbard-model physics, including the Mott insulator in 3D optical lattices, fermionic Mott states, and quantum gas microscopy, gives controllable access to correlated-electron models that theory cannot solve classically. It connects directly to the physics I care about.
assessment.attribution: Greiner-Bloch (superfluid-Mott transition, 2002), Esslinger (fermionic Mott insulator, 2008) and Greiner's microscope are central. The Jaksch-Zoller proposal is credited in the list, but I keep the experiment trio; however Zoller and Cirac may be considered separately via their own entry.
assessment.maturity: Many groups confirm and extend; fermionic Hubbard simulations are now beyond classical reach in some regimes. Still evolving toward a decisive solved problem, though the technique is established.
uncertainties: Uncertain whether the central discovery is the bosonic Mott transition (partly overlapping with the 2001 BEC prize area) or the fermionic simulation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave photons a practical architecture, and underlies most superconducting quantum processors. Timely following the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory, 2004), Wallraff (first strong-coupling experiment, 2004) and Schoelkopf (Yale group, transmon, readout) is a coherent theory-plus-experiment set; Michel Devoret and others contributed deeply to the field but are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and widely replicated; the physics is established. There is risk the committee views this as engineering of a platform recently recognised by the 2025 prize.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2025 prize reduces appetite for another superconducting-circuit award.
Credit boundaries between qubit design (transmon) and cQED are unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opened new tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a precision-measurement achievement based on clean quantum mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic wavelength lattice clock and Ye brought it to the best performance; a two-person configuration is clean, though other strong clock groups (ion clocks, Hall and Haensch for combs) mean the field's credit will be discussed.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in several laboratories, with accuracy beyond the SI second; a redefinition of the second is under discussion. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: This is outside my core area, so I defer to colleagues in atomic physics on relative standing.
Overlap in credit with ion-clock and frequency-comb contributions.
